evidence: Only one top-level package ('modules') with flat structure (max directory depth = 2)
Main script 'darkscrape.py' contains high-level orchestration logic and imports modules directly
Modules (file.py, url.py) contain mixed responsibilities (e.g., file parsing + URL handling + face recognition)
No clear separation into layers (e.g., no distinct data, business, UI layers)
Functional-style modules with global procedures ( functions like 'scrap', 'main', 'banner')
Very low fan-out (avg=3.5) and minimal cross-module dependencies
All modules live in one directory without clear architectural boundaries
risks: Tight coupling between modules due to shared imports and overlapping responsibilities (e.g., 'face_re' function appears in both modules)
Hard to test individual components in isolation due to lack of interfaces or dependency injection
Limited scalability and maintainability as functionality grows
Violation of single responsibility principle in modules
